intro.heading: Our own products, as case studies
intro.text: These are products we built for ourselves and for people we know. Each page shows real screens from a working copy, and every figure carries the system it came from and the date it was read.

studies.title: A 1,900-lesson sales course with an AI coach, built in under an hour and a half
studies.teaser: Felicia's Sales Sanctum: a private course that teaches one calm way of selling, with a chat tutor, a role-play partner that scores her and a speech coach, all on a phone.

brief.heading: The brief
points: A private place for one learner, Felicia, to learn a calm, honest way of selling from first call to close.
It had to work on her phone first, with a login only she has.
It had to teach by doing: read a lesson, answer a quiz, practise on a pretend customer, hear how she sounds.

built.name: The course
built.text: 1,900 lessons in 190 modules. Every lesson has a short read, key points, a worked example, a five question quiz and a practice task.

built.name: A chat tutor
built.text: Ask a question in plain words and get an answer that points back to the exact lessons that cover it.

built.name: A role-play partner
built.text: A pretend customer with a personality pushes back. Type score and she gets a mark out of 5 with one thing to fix next time.

built.name: A speech coach
built.text: She records herself, the recording is turned into text on the server, and the coach comments on pace and wording.

built.name: Progress that sticks
built.text: Quizzes are marked on the server, so progress and points cannot be faked from the phone. Modules open in order.

how.heading: How it was built
paragraphs: The course was written by a fleet of AI workers from one written specification, then joined into a single course folder. The app around it is a small server with no moving parts to look after.

The AI replies in the screenshots below are stand-in text. The pictures come from a local run with no AI model attached, so you see the real screens, the real lessons and the real quiz marking, with a fixed sentence where the live coach would speak.

studies.title: A second course track, 1,800 lessons on building with AI, added to a live learning app in one day
studies.teaser: Pala's Build with AI track teaches a complete beginner to build real things with AI from scratch, inside the app she already uses, with her own tutor beside every lesson.

brief.heading: The brief
points: Pala had finished a first track and wanted the next one: how to build with AI, from nothing.
It had to live inside the app she already knows, with its own progress and its own switcher.
It had to teach by doing: read, answer, then try it with the tutor.

built.name: A new track
built.text: 1,800 lessons in 180 modules, each with a short read, a worked example, a five question quiz and a try-it task.

built.name: A track switcher
built.text: The first track and the new one sit side by side, each with its own progress, so nothing she already earned was touched.

built.name: Petal, her tutor
built.text: A tutor on every screen that answers in plain words and links back to the lessons that cover the question.

built.name: Help me ask this well
built.text: A button that coaches her on how to write a better question or prompt before she sends it.

how.heading: How it was built
paragraphs: The track was written by a fleet of AI workers from one specification and joined into the app a module at a time. A checker refused any module that failed, so one bad lesson could not stall the rest.
The screenshots come from a local run with no AI model attached, so the tutor's replies are stand-in text. The lessons, the quiz marking and the screens are the real ones.

studies.title: The TITANOS HUD: our own build, counted live in public
studies.teaser: A public page where every number about how we build is read from our own logs, labelled measured or modelled, with a feed of finished jobs that names no client.

brief.heading: The brief
points: Show how fast and how safely we build, without asking anyone to take our word for it.
Separate what we measured from what we modelled, on the page, every time.
Never show a client or a job that names one.

built.name: An engineering counter
built.text: Lines of code, commits and tests, each with its label and its source.

built.name: A tachometer
built.text: Work output against the modelled ceiling, so the gap between what we do and what we could do is visible.

built.name: A compute panel
built.text: Jobs, median job time and failure rate for the worker fleet over the last 24 hours.

built.name: A receipt feed
built.text: A live list of finished jobs by category word and codename only. Jobs that name an organisation are dropped before the page sees them.

how.heading: How it was built
paragraphs: A script exports the numbers ledger into one file at build time, and the page reads only that file, so the page cannot drift from the ledger. A second file feeds the receipt list, and the browser refreshes it every minute.
A test fails the build if any organisation or person word appears in the feed.
